name: dancing lights
sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Fairy lights describe the sight of trouping fairies on the move. The fairies travel from one otherworld dance hall to another. They move in great processions. Each figure carries a torch above their head. Fairies are smaller than humans. People saw the parades as twinkling lights. The lights streamed along invisible but always-straight pathways. The path stayed straight wherever the band passed. The procession moved across the land at night. Observers mistook the small glowing band for scattered points of light.

okr.objective: This record documents fairy lights as the folkloric sight of trouping fairies travelling in torchlit procession.
key_results: Trouping fairies move between otherworld dance halls in procession.
Each fairy carries a torch above its head.
Humans see the small figures as twinkling lights.
The processions follow invisible but always-straight pathways.
